output.name: Sarvi
output.myth: Ennu the Kite-Wright made the first bridled kite for Aun, who asked how a thing might hold still in a gale. She cut the cloth from an old sail, stretched it on whalebone, and tied one knot in the bridle so the wind would have something to pull against. Tavo the Gale came down the cliff laughing and tore off the tail in one shake. So Ennu tied long ribbons to the corners and let them hang. A kite that is all sail goes nowhere. It needs weight to hang from. Aun flew it until the line ran out, and that is how he learned the sky was far. When he cut the string, that kite went aloft first. It hangs over Vel now, and north of it the Gull That Fell Back watches with her own torn tail, since Tavo took hold of hers too. Further off, the Mended Gull hangs where Ennu sewed her up. Hesk counts the knots on the Reel and says the bridle is still tied. Hang your ribbons low when you fly. The wind reads them.
output.finding: Find Sekra, the Gull That Fell Back, then look a little under one hand-span (about 16°) south of her to find Sarvi, the Bridled Kite.
